en.site_tagline: Free rice tools, prices & rice knowledge
en.footer_about: rice.ag is a free, independent project: a rice grain scanner, a moisture calculator, daily rice prices and plain-language rice guides. Tools are free to use; photos are analysed on your device and never uploaded.
en.footer_disclaimer: Results are estimates for quick checks and are not a substitute for laboratory grading or official inspection certificates.
en.sc_intro: Photograph a spread-out rice sample, and get an instant estimate of whole vs. broken kernels, grain size & shape, colour consistency, and suspect foreign objects. Everything runs in your browser.
en.sc_coin_hint: Place one coin flat, away from the grains. Enables mm measurements and the 1.4 mm chip rule.
en.sc_known_hint: Leave empty to estimate from the sample. Requires a coin.
en.sc_privacy: Your photo never leaves your device. Analysis runs locally in your browser; nothing is uploaded or stored.
en.sc_empty: Your annotated photo will appear here.
en.sc_breakdown_note: Classes follow ISO 7301 / Codex STAN 198 length definitions, relative to the average whole-kernel length in this sample. Weight share is estimated from projected area.
en.sc_consistency_hint: share of kernels within ΔE 6 of the sample's typical colour
en.sc_colour_note: Colour values depend on your camera and light. Compare samples photographed with the same setup.
en.sc_chalk_need: Chalkiness needs a backlit photo (grains on a lightbox or phone screen showing white). Normal top-lit photos can't separate chalky from translucent rice reliably.
en.sc_flags_note: Flags are for human review. Rice-coloured stones can look exactly like grains in a photo, so a clean result does not prove a sample is stone-free.
en.fl_redBrown: Red / brown (red rice, bran, paddy, husk?)
en.w_lowContrast: Low contrast between grains and background. Use a matte black cloth or card and even light.
en.w_lightBackgroundInDarkMode: The background looks light. Grains on white paper are hard to separate — use a dark background, or switch to lightbox mode if the grains are backlit.
en.w_darkBackgroundInBacklitMode: Lightbox mode is selected but the background looks dark.
en.w_coinNotFound: No coin found. Place one coin flat and apart from the grains, fully inside the photo.
en.w_edgeCut: Several grains are cut off at the photo edge and were excluded. Keep the whole sample inside the frame.
en.w_manyClumps: Many grains are touching and were excluded. Spread the grains so they don't touch.
en.w_smallSample: Fewer than 100 kernels measured. Percentages from small samples can swing a lot; aim for 200–300 kernels.
en.w_lowResolution: Grains are small in the photo. Move closer or crop so each grain is at least ~40 pixels long.
en.e_noObjects: No grains found. Check that the grains are on a contrasting background and in focus.
en.e_tooFew: Too few grains found to analyse.
en.e_load: Couldn't read that image. Try a JPG or PNG.
en.sc_time: Analysed {n} objects in {ms} ms at {w}×{h} px.
en.sc_scale: Scale: {mm} mm per pixel from a {d} mm coin.
en.sc_noscale: No size reference: lengths are relative. Add a coin for millimetres.
en.sc_wf_title: Need rice that scores well every time?
en.sc_wf_body: Wildfield grows and mills 100% single-variety Chainat-1 for noodle makers, with lot-level traceability from farm to bag.
en.mc_intro: Two quick checks for paddy trading: the weight you should end up with after drying, and the moisture your drying records imply.
en.mc_a_title: A. Weight after drying to a target moisture
en.mc_b_title: B. Moisture implied by drying records
en.mc_note: Formula: dry matter = weight × (1 − moisture). Dry matter stays constant through drying except for handling losses.
